files.why: Add a pure, framework-free invoice filter predicate (e.g. filterInvoices/matchesInvoiceQuery) — which fields count as a match is domain knowledge, so it lives in core and stays unit-testable without Vue.
Own a reactive search `query` ref, debounce it via shared useDebounce, and expose the filtered invoice list to the view (search UI state belongs in the ui composable).
Render the <Input> search box (existing shared primitive) bound to the composable's query, above the invoices table.
Cover the new pure invoice filter predicate (matches/no-match, case-insensitivity, empty query).
Add a pure, framework-free appointment filter predicate mirroring billing's — kept duplicated per slice, not promoted to shared (rule 7: only 2 usages).
Own a debounced search `query` ref and expose a filtered appointments list alongside the existing day/conflict state.
Render the <Input> search box bound to the composable's query, above the appointment list.
Cover the new pure appointment filter predicate.

uncertain: Placement of the filter predicate: I put it in each slice's core/rules.ts because 'which fields match' is domain knowledge and belongs to framework-free, deletable-if-Vue-dies logic. It is borderline — a case could be made for keeping trivial substring filtering inside the ui composable. I leaned core for testability and purity.

Duplicating the predicate in both slices rather than a shared helper: intentional per constitution rule 7 (3+ same-reason usages before promotion to shared/lib; two usages stay duplicated). Confident but flagging the deliberate non-DRY choice.

Whether to touch the central tests/*.core.test.ts files as part of this change vs. leaving them to a follow-up — I included them because a real feature needs regression coverage and that folder is the established home for core tests.
No index.ts changes: the search filter is intra-slice (ui -> own core), so nothing new needs to cross a slice's public surface. I'm fairly sure, assuming client-side filtering (see questions).
questions: Client-side or server-side search? Both lists already load their FULL dataset once (billing caches all invoices in the Pinia store via ensureLoaded; scheduling fetches all appointments then filters by day in memory). So 'filters as you type without hammering the server' is naturally satisfied by in-memory filtering + a debounced input, with NO new query/DTO/MSW work. If you actually want server-side search (a `?q=` param), that changes the file list substantially (billing/data/queries.ts + store.ts, scheduling/data/queries.ts, each slice's data/dto.ts + mappers.ts + mocks.ts) — which do you intend?

Scheduling has no human-readable text field to search: an Appointment carries only opaque ids (clientId, resourceId), a status, and start/end times — there's no name/number like an invoice has. What should the appointment search actually match on, and do we need to resolve/display client or resource names first (which would pull in more data)?
For invoices, which fields should the search match — invoice `number` only, or also status / client? And is it case-insensitive substring, or prefix?
Is the shared useDebounce default of 300ms the desired delay, or do you have a specific debounce interval in mind?
